problem:

A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 & 5 \\ -1 & 2 & 7\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix given above. Identify **all** of the reasons why one can conclude that $|A|=0?$

- $A$ has proportional columns
- $A$ has identical columns
- $A$ has identical rows

choices.value: None of the statements are true

activity_context.topic_title: Conditions When a Determinant Equals Zero

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} & 1 & 5 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 4 \\ \sqrt{5} & 1 & 5 & 2 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

 
Consider the matrix given above. Identify **all** of the reasons why one can conclude that $|A|=0?$

- $A$ has a zero row
- $A$ has two proportional columns
- $A$ has two identical rows
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the statements in turn.

- $A$ does *not* have a zero row.

- $A$ has two proportional columns:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} & 1 & 5 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 4 \\ \sqrt{5} & 1 & 5 & 2 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & 8\end{aligned}]\,✓
$$

- $A$ has two identical rows: 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} & 1 & 5 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 & 4 \\ \sqrt{5} & 1 & 5 & 2 \\ -1 & 4 & -1 & 8\end{aligned}]\,✓
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
